title: Don’t waste your time with Google Calendar App
body:
Online/Conputer version is great. App if horrible.  Don’t waste your time with the app unless you only want to visually see your appointments. Entering is worthless. 

I’ll only state two issues:

1) You can’t copy and paste and event/appointment on the app. You can only move it. So if you’re entering an appointment that you’ve had before you have to re-enter all the details from scratch.  Waste of time. You can do this directly in google via a computer, but the feature is not available on the app.

2) People that need a calendar app are typically busy people with multiple parts of their lives. It’s great the google allows you to create multiple calendars for different activities. However you can only do that online via a computer. When you create an event/appointment in the app there is no option to decide which calendar you’re creating the event for.

I could go critique the app some more, but these 2 features, which are easily done if you have a computer and are signed into google, do not carry over to the app. They are essential features. Soo essential and intuitive that when you first get the app you send lots of time looking for where the features would be because you would never think that they don’t exist on the app. You literally find yourself scratching your head as to why the features aren’t there. It basically renders the app as just a tool to view your events and nothing else.

title: Everything one might need in a calendar app
body: I love how Google Calendar automagically uploads everything to the cloud. I also love how it suggests locations based on the address one types in (of course it doesn't do this for private addresses, but it is still a handy feature.) It will set reminders by month, day, hour, or minute, and it also asks if one wants to set up recurring appointments for a number of weeks, a number of days, or annually (handy for Birthday reminders.) The app will also convert between time zones across the world—another useful feature. And all of these can easily be set whether one is using a smartphone or a tablet, and also a desktop or a laptop. All of the changes are sent to the cloud, as well. It is possible to export it into many other formats as well, such as iCal, and Microsoft Office. I ❤️ Google Calendar and will continue to use it until they pry it out of my hands. 🙂

title: I'm a convert
body: Of all the e-calendars that I've tried, I like Google calendar the best. I actually have preferred a paper date book and always end up returning to paper.  In fact I recently purchased a 2018 date book, then a 2017-18 academic year date book before deciding that I really needed to lighten my load and use a calendar on my phone since my phone is always with me.  I don't like the iPhone calendar app.   Used that for a couple of years.  I tried Outlook for a brief time.  It was better than the iPhone calendar, but I found Outlook to be cumbersome and confusing.  Google calendar is super easy to use, has some nice features, and I don't feel bombarded with too many bells and whistles that I don't need.  I'm sure the fancy stuff is there for those who need to do more complicated calendar things.  One thing though that is super easy is adding a location to your event.  I tried it for an event at a location that I'd never been to -- so simple! It practically added itself.  Another thing:  it added airline departure information that it picked up from one of my emails.  Of course, if you don't like that "how does it know what I'm doing " feeling, you can adjust what to allow in the settings.

body: Google calendar will put departure times in your calendar, taking them from your emails from for example expedia. But while expedia will give you the departure time from Rome based on the time in Rome, Google calendar changes the departure time based on whatever time zone you happen to be in. If you change the time zone your departure time to Rome then the Google time will be correct again, but then your arrival time will be wrong, or any connecting flights in between. They have had this problem for years, but prefer to spend their money on self-drving cars instead of fixing this mess. Worse, these days when you put the correct departure time in yourself, THEY ALSO CHANGE IT!!!

Next issue...google adds images to certain types of appointments that take up the whole time block. These make my calendar much kore cumbersome as I use the colors of different calendars to see what's happening at a glance in my day. When I have a dentist appointment on the calendar for one of my family members I have to either look for the tiny color coded line at the bottom of the large time block, click the event to see who's calendar it's on or change views to one too small to have the image I DON'T WANT. Fixing these issues would bring my rating up substantially.

title: Almost perfect
body:
Google made a great calendar app with all the views you could want: agenda, day, 3 day, week, and month. Perfect. The ability to switch accounts is also nice. Repeating events. Check. Invitee options. It's there. Notifications work well from what I can tell.

I just have a couple of nitpicky items.

1. Please rename the app to something that fits in the iOS app name field on the iPhone. Right now it shows "Google Cal...", which is a little sloppy in my opinion. Gcal? Google Cal? Just Calendar? I'm not sure, but it would look much cleaner.

2. Please implement a dynamic icon that shows the current date instead of a static "31". I know this is just recently possible so I'll cut some slack for that.

Otherwise it's a great app! Good job Google!

title: Solid Calendar apt for busy and not so busy people
body:
I have never been a fan of the native iPhone calendar app. So I have spent many hours reviewing my options.  My biggest complaint with most apps is the weekly view is always grid based with time on he left. For those of us with few appointments, or apts. at hours spanning the day and night, this required one to constantly scroll up and down through empty, unscheduled time as you scrolled left and right through the week. 

iCalendar by Reedle solved this with their weekly block view which showed appointments in blocks right next to each other for a given day of the week, with no unscheduled time hogging up space in the screen. In an instant I can easily see days that are free and days that have scheduled blocks.

Google calendar solves this as well with their Schedule view. Showing blocks for appointments in a feed type format. One downside is that since they only list appointments it is sometimes hard to figure out what days are completely free, since it will show a appointment block for Monday and right under it the next apt let's say on Friday with no visual gap, so it's not an easy visual to see which days are completely open. Not a huge issue, it just make one have to think and not just see instantly. 

I do love the images it used to convey the appointments. It adds some flair to a usually boring visual screen of a calendar.

I wish I didn't have to click on the "edit" button to edit it but simply tap it. That's two additional taps to change a schedule. Also, if I write, "lunch with GM at 12pm," it'd be nice if the app intuitively set the time to 12pm to 1pm. 

The design is also a bit confusing to look at. I had to scroll and focus really hard to find the "Location" to at my location. I do appreciate that it uses Google Maps to direct me to my location when I click on it. 

Lastly, it'd be great if there was a Mac app that would allow me to use it apart from the browser.

title: More Convoluted Than Necessary
body:
We should be able to set month view as the permanent view. Currently it's not, it's set up really confusing and non functional right now. I want to see the month, and add notes to the month, without it ever zooming into the day. My computer's Google Calendar allows this and it's much nicer. Please stop forcing us to micro manage our days by zooming into the day or making us write exact start and end times. I only use calendars to see what I did on a certain day, or to see future plans. I don't want to map out every minute of my day.

For example: I work on Wednesday, then I play volleyball. I would write those two things out on my calendar. I know the start and end times by heart, so writing every minute detail into the app is an annoyance. All I want to see is what I am supposed to do or what I did. It is more convenient for me to write start and end times in the titles, rather than scroll through to select day, hour, minute, am/pm, followed by making sure there was no input errors. Please appease those of us that aren't micromanagers but want to also stay organized.

title: Get it together, already, Google.
body:
This app could be so much better, if Google would actually give half a crap.  For one thing, it's absolutely shameful that the app icon STILL doesn't reflect the current date -- iCal can even do that, FFS.  The app is buggy AF, too.  Most of the time I open it, it hangs, or it takes tens of seconds before it responds to any touch commands (and with this latest update, it crashes...awesome).  Once you've created an event and saved it, you can't change which calendar it belongs to in edit mode; you can change its color, but not the calendar in which it appears.  You can't copy events from one day to another.  You can't differentiate visually between an all-day event and an event with a specific time while viewing your calendars in monthly mode.  You can't enter a location that draws information from your contacts.  You can't add it to your widgets.  You can't.  You can't.  You can't.

I want to like this app, but Google are making it impossible by not fixing obvious issues or adding common sense features.  Until they do, I'm switching to Readdle's Calendars.

title: Good start
body:
This calendar is the best of the many trials I've done over the last 5+ years. The bright colors make it easy to categorize events for our family of 6 & my office tasks. I also like that it syncs with my desktop calendar. 

Some problem features: there needs to be an easier way to "invite" others to an event. My husband & I don't need to share all tasks - but there are many that we do both need to see. It's tedious to add him to each event. There should be a quick default invite for "favorites". 

Also the way it appears on the desktop makes my head spin. I wish it showed month to month & CLEARLY highlighted the current week when viewing. When I scroll the month-view it's so hard to see the day of the month & it keeps shifting & showing part of 2 months at a time. Why not just have the 28-31 days of the month showing?? 

For this reason I avoid the desktop version to manage the schedule - though I would have used it were it easy for a 4Oish year old to see (even on my large Mac screen!)

I also wish the options for notifications could be set for my preferences. I don't want emails. 

Lastly- the ability to repeat events needs to be improved. I want to repeat on irregular days (i.e., bball April 2,7,10,18 etc.).

title: No Badge App Icons!! :/
body: I used to use Google Calendar as my only calendar and reminder app. I always had Android phones, and your reminders would remain in your status bar until you dismissed them. But when I switched over to Apple, there are no status bar reminders, you have to open the Notification Center to see everything. However, all of the apps have these convenient little red numbers on them when you haven't dealt with something in the app yet, so those are your reminders. Lamentably, Google Calendar is the ONLY app I have downloaded that doesn't have this feature. And since in the absence of status bar reminders I have come to rely so heavily on these tiny red numbers, I do not find Google Calendar preferable anymore. I could link it to Apple Calendar, but then I'd be using two apps to do the job one should be able to do. So I just started using the Apple Reminders app instead. I miss Google Calendar, but until they fix this issue, I can no longer use it :/

title: Jcessenwein
body: There's only one problem with Google Calendar for IPhone, but it's so easy to overcome that it didn't affect my star rating: You can't change the notification sound to make Google Calendar actually notify you with more than a beep. The solution? Link it with your Apple Calendar. You can link just the calendar you want, so you don't get notifications for "just Facebook Friends'" birthdays or holidays. AND you can share individual calendars with people (like coworkers) to help keep everyone on the same page. Plus, the color coding is very helpful, especially having default colors for different calendars. And you can save locations to your events and just click on the location to open Google Maps (or even Waze or Apple Maps).

title: So want to love it, but.....

1. Would love to simplify the agenda view. An option for black font against white would greatly help folks with vision impairments. Also it would be great to be able to change the font size. 

2. Whenever there is an address entered into the address window the schedule view background for that appointment has a map view. Is there a way to disable this?  This makes the appointment details hard to view and confusing to look at, like I'm referring to in my first point. (Developers, I would recommend giving your phone to someone older and let them take this app for a test run). They will give you similar feedback. 

3. With the schedule view background in mind, sometimes that view defaults to  generic clip art, which usually corresponds to the name of the appointment. For example "bike ride" is the appointment name and your app gives me a schedule view that has a bike. Again, this makes for a confusing view of the schedule. Is there a way to disable this feature so that the view is more simple and classic?

Thanks

This is unfortunate because I really prefer the Apple Calendar app. Why would Google arbitrarily choose to have "31" rather than the actual date on the app icon? I also find the Apple calendar to be easier to navigate and the calendar colors are true/consistent across the spectrum, where my Google calendar appointments are varied colors dependent on if I open up the web based or app version of the calendar. I also like how the Apple app was intelligently designed to adapt to the size of the screen where the Google app prefers to cut off names of calendar events to instead provide wasted space for overly large axis headers for time and date. I also have to turn off the notification for each individual calendar event rather than choosing to turn on a notification if needed. I'm really disappointed with the app so far and hope some changes are planned for the future.

title: Excellent
body:
For any person who is looking to better organize their life to live more productive, Google Calendar is the way to go. Not only can you share your calendar with others but you can create a calendar with shared owners. You can have events repeat as many times as you like, with different options like bi-weekly, repeating more than one week a day, etc. 

One thing I would change is having the default setting to only send notifications. Right now, or at least the last time I checked, google calendar starts off with sending you emails and notifications. To turn off emails you have to go into the calendar setting and change it or for each event you make you have to turn off the emails option (which can be tedious). 

Overall, Google Calendar has been a great addition to my life structure and I use it pretty much 24/7 to update events, make sure I am doing everything I needed to for the day, looking ahead to prepare myself for the next day/week/month/year, etc. 

You never realize how much you can accomplish in a day until you plan it out!

title: Pretty on the eyes, but not very smart
body:
It's easy to use if you are not required by your organization to use it daily. I prefer to use my computer browser to schedule meetings/appointments and inform others of my availability. When I need to check where I am going next, it is a nice looking and easy tool for an on the go planner - especially since it syncs with the schedule that I input online. Unfortunately, it is a pain to use the app to input the schedule.
The options available on a browse afford you much more options for creating events. The app does attempt to be smart -- It allows you to just type in the information on a single line and then will organize the information in to the correct categories,but it doesn't always work correctly.
I love this app despite all of that. The way Google has woven this beautiful quilt of applications, services, and utilities together is beautiful and sometimes I wonder how we ever got along with other their platform.
For the individual, or for an organization of thousands, the Google system is the only thing that I recommend if you want to use the internet with your computer/phone is 1. Chrome Browser 2. Gmail 3. Google Drive 4. Google Calendar 5. Google fpcs/slides/sheets /forms 6. Google play + the Google Apps that fit your needs for entertainment (music, books, games, TV, etc.).

Google has it all. They're a great company that has made a free version of all our favorite products - that even work seamlessly with our favorite products.

No longer can an underprivileged student suffer through high school because they can't afford $120+ for Microsoft Office  at home! Just log onto your Google account and use docs. Or go to a WiFi hotshot to acquire the offline, desktop version of Google docs!

It's brilliant and I love Google. Oh and did I mention that they have a computer that DREAMS? 

Another note: Google Drive has made my research collaborations easier than ever before and with my colleagues using Google Calendar, scheduling face to face meetings and video conferences is easier than breathing.

Forget doctor appointments easily? Don't like to allow push notifications from apps? Never fear, Google Calendar us here. Just select your preferred notification type and how long before the appointment you need to be reminded. When I have an important appointment that I may forget, then I just have Google Calendar send me a text message. AMAZING!

Use this app. Or use another one for a month so that when you finally get Google Calendar, you will be able to appreciate the world's best time management tool - for Free.

title: Decent app, but needs to include obvious functionality
body:
I like the app - colorful, quick, and mostly intuitive. However, it lacks some really obvious functions:
- calendar app on the iPhone shows the date on the app icon; why can't Google Calendar do this?
- you can't grab and drag an appointment to a different time or day! You have to go in to the appointment and change the day/time
- you can't snooze the Google Calendar notification from the lock screen
- new appointment defaults to last type used and this can't be changed. 

I'm sure others have mentioned these deficits before, but I think they're worth repeating. 

Things I like:
- syncs more quickly and accurately with my online Google Calendars
- can add a depth of detail to the appointments that can't be done with the iPhone calendar 
- integrates beautifully with other Google apps

title: Love it!
body:
I was thrilled when Google finally made an iPhone app for their calendar. I like to have my calendar synced on both my computer at work and home and on my phone, and as far I know, there wasn't a quick and easy way to access my iCal on my work computer, which resulted in my switch to Google Calendar. My one big problem with the Google Calendar app was that it lacked a whole-month view of all scheduled events. Now, that problem is solved!! HALLELUJAH!! Thank you, Google! I'm so happy to see this feature! 

I also love the reminder feature, but I wish that the app would alert me when a reminder comes up without my having to open  the app to check. 

My only other suggestion for improvement would be to add a feature that allows users to copy events to different dates. I know you can set an event to repeat. I want the ability to quickly add an often but irregularly recurring event. For example, if a person has several doctor's appointments scheduled at the same doctor's office over the course of a few months, I wish you were able to enter the appointment name and location once and then specify the recurring dates and times at the same time (without going in to create separate events), before clicking "save" once to save all appointments. That may be asking a lot, but this would make the app TOP NOTCH! 

Thanks again, Google, and keep the updates coming!

body:

 I HATE(!!!) the background photos on events. I add a map or dinner event & there is a either a picture of location/map or a plate setting. It's distracting and I usually skip over those events because they are out of place and not in my chosen color. Please get rid of these. I cannot stress that enough. body: I was a huge fan of the app Timeful which Google bought a little while ago. It's nice to see some of the features of that being implemented through Goals. Otherwise they just sit there and I never notice/do them (pretty much the main main thing Timeful was out to solve). I would also like to be able to reschedule an event just by dragging it around. title: Can't figure out conference calls
body: I'm pretty surprised that with the wealth of development talent that Google supposedly has at their behest, they can't figure out how to integrate a conference call line as the location with the phone.  Half the time it suggests that I dial the number with no pauses, sometimes it includes pauses but no pound signs, and seemingly about half the time it tries to open Maps to tell me it doesn't know where the meeting is.  Apple calendar has worked for years with phone lines, MobileDay has worked for years, even more challenging since it introspects the invite to try to figure out lines and codes.  Why Google hasn't been able to figure this out is beyond me.  But since the majority of my meetings are on conference lines, that basically makes the app useless to me as a productivity aid.  Yes, it can show me a meeting, so two stars, which I think is exceptionally generous.

title: Best College Planner! Goals feature!!!
body: Trying to plan around work, college, and everything in between is usually very stressful. Most apps just give me a headache as other calendars make me feel like holding my phone up all the way to my face and my other notification apps don't always remind me. On the computer this is a great app, and it syncs automatically and best onto mobile version compared to other crossover apps. Better yet, it has a completely different look on different devices which makes it easy to use (on PC you can choose between views: weekly, monthly, etc. On phone you can see compacted daily-weekly chores and easily swipe up/down to view other days). At first I missed the monthly/weekly viewing option common with PC and other mobile apps, but the most important feature for this daily version to work (a banner which lets you select the month) is always at the top of the screen, and adding events is simple, whether rehearsals three days a week for three weeks every other month or an appointment you found out about 2 hours prior, thanks to the big blatant red button always on-screen (it retains the click-to-add feature from PC if you blow up any particular day) and wide range of scheduling repeat options. Even if you forget to set an alarm/notification you'll automatically get a reminder 10 min before every event. Very simple but aesthetically pleasing Google look (and as always you can color code). Best app I've used so far and the only one I'll use in the future. The goals feature surprised me: if you need to get something done a few times a week, every day, etc., but don't know when you'll have the time(I.e. Studying, cleaning, practicing), this app will ask what you want to do, when in the day you'd prefer to do it (mornings, evenings, afternoons, any of the above), and for how long, and then schedule the best time for you! If a goal interferes with a new event it will recalculate and reschedule accordingly, that same day if possible!

title: Great for college
body:
I love having a calendar on my phone. As a pharmacy student, I have lots going on. I use this app in conjunction with GCalendar on my laptop, and that makes it great. I can set up and organize classes and assignments on my laptop, and then take a look at what I have coming up on my phone. It is easy to set up, synchs quickly, and is easy to look at. I am very satisfied with my experience so far. 
However, there is one thing I would like to see different. Some complain about there not being a month view on the app. My calendar is cluttered just for a few days- a month view on my phone would be too small to read if it fit everything on it. (By the way, tapping the top left allows you to jump to any day you want.) What I would like to see, for the web browser and if possible on the phone, is a button to choose what you see on the month view. Right now, on any given day there are at least 5 things per day. It would be cool if I could choose one or two of those to be present on the month view, and the rest hidden. So, I could see the deadline next week, or the exam in a few days, without sifting through all my classes and readings and labs and so on.

title: Almost perfect
body: My first app was the one by Readdle. Looked for an updated app and found this over a year ago. Love it! It is so easy to fill out details for events with the auto-complete feature. I would find it too laborious to do in my other calendar (so would just put in the basics), but here is just click, click, click! Can even invite other people. The graphics were an unexpected delight; it will add a photo of the restaurant or an icon for eating out, getting hair cut, etc. The thing that originally drew me to it was the flight auto-compete. Detects confirmation e-mails and the flight info goes right into the calendar! I don't know what other people are saying about can't pick which calendar it goes to - you certainly can. There are so many features, you just have to play around. The only reason I don't give 5 stars is that there is NO monthly view! I thought I saw promise of this when I first got the app, but nothing. That's just rotten. So, I have to keep my Readdle app and flip to it any time I want to schedule hair appointment, meeting with friends, doc or vet appt, -- anything that requires that long-view. When will you make this feature availaboe????? (Yes, you do have to go to the computer to create a new calendar, but I don't find that to be a problem. The colors sync and I can choose to display, hide, or schedule with any calendar on my list)

title: Happiness, with some suggestions
body:
I was stumbling through the App Store, trying to recover from the news that my favorite calendar app-Sunrise-was being deleted, when I found out that Google has FINALLY created a calendar app for iOS!! Yes!! This has been too log in coming! Google is incredibly innovative and intuitive, and I couldn't function without their other apps! I am so pleased to find this calendar app, and in the five minutes I've been able to use it, am quite happy. I do, however, have a couple of suggestions for updates. 
1.) It would be helpful to have an option to "anchor" the monthly view in place, so that it is visible as you scroll through your schedule/daily/weekly view at the bottom. Very helpful. Sooooo helpful. 
2.) if the thumbnail icon for the app could reflect the current day's date (as opposed to the "31" it currently sports) it would be fantastic. 

That's it. That's all I want. Get me those things, and we're in 5-star territory!

title: Good app but needs more sharing options.Needs to sync bdays from my phone Contacts.
body:
Good app. Love the illustrations, the colors, syncing events from gmail 

1️⃣ I would like to sync with events I see in my browser or a message. I know I can do it if there is a date listed because it makes it a link to google calendar. But I want to see it as an option on the browser's "Share" options (where it says share through "Message, Mail, Notes, save as PDF etc"). There should be an option to "create event in Google Calendar" or add to Google calendar. So I can chose whether to add it as an Event or To-Do reminder. 

2️⃣ It needs to show the current date on the front of the app icon (like Apple's calendar). It is a very convenient feature so I can see the current date right there on my home page instead of swiping my notifications tab.

3️⃣ needs a month view so I can see what days are free and the number of events I have scheduled that day. Or the amount of hours I have "free"

4️⃣ birthdays from my phone Contacts should be able to be synced into Google calendar. I don't have all my current contacts in gmail.
 
5️⃣ want to be able to change the calendar that an event is listed under after I have created the event. 

6️⃣ needs a landscape mode for better viewing!

Otherwise app would be great! 👍

title: Good, but needs improvement
body:
The good:
1.  Intuitive.
2.  Easy to use.
3.  Painlessly syncs across devices.
4.  Grabs events from emails.

Improvements needed:
1.  Landscape on iPad.
2.  Smaller fonts / ability to select size on iPad.
3.  Put current date on icon.  "31" is on the icon all the time.  You might as well put a picture of a turnip, which is a disgusting vegtable that no one likes.
4.  Month view.  The lack of a month view begs for a snide comment, but its absence leaves me speechless.

While the ability to grab events like flights from emails is nifty, I've put events in other calendar aps for a long time and wrote them on paper calendars before that.  I view smaller fonts and month view as more important.  Lack of month view is like a car without heat / air.  It runs, but doesn't feel very good.

title: Needs work
body:
There's a lot to love about Google calendar. It's beautiful and syncs fast. But coming from Sunrise, I noticed some deficiencies as well that need to be addressed. 

First, it isn't clear to me when invitations are sent or received. This was very clear in Sunrise. 

Second, the summarized location information is a terrible idea. What if I want to meet a friend at a coffee shop and they have 2 locations close to each other. Typing in the name, I have to guess because they are both listed identically. I can only commit and repeat if I guess.incorrectly. 

Finally, the reminders implementation needs work. Sorting by time? Nope. If you add a note to an email, you can only see the note. 'Open in Inbox' opens Inbox and does *NOT* go to the actual reminder. (And there aren't any reminder sort options, which totally stinks.)

I love Google Calendar for the desktop and it works great. I'm hoping the mobile team takes the feedback in stride and gets the details right.

title: Goals do not properly register as completed

1.) when you mark a goal done, a success notification pops up and the goal has a strikethrough the text, but this disappears quickly and the goal is marked not done

2.) in Timeful, when you marked a task done (whether goal or one off todo item), a completed time block would appear at the time you clicked "done". It was my understanding that they used the "time completed" data to help schedule future goals and todos. In this app, to change the time of a goal session, you have to click the goal, change session time, click ok, then mark as done (4 clicks, you serious???)

To start, it has extremely busy, way too cutesy monthly views that look more like a list than an actually monthly overview. I tried to give some other features a shot so I switched to a weekly view. To get the whole week in view the app makes your events so small you can't even read what you have typed down. So I switched to 3 day view which was better but I'd really like to see my whole week. Long story short, all the other features failed in comparison to iCal so for me, it's not worth switching. This review gets a 1 star because the app works and I was able to import my iCal calendar with ease. But it's just to busy to see your events clearly.

title: Very useful and could be better than IPhone's default, but lacking.
body: This app is amazing and I enjoy using it far more than IPhone's default calendar, but their are two things that come to mind as I writ this that would make it without a doubt my number one choice over the Apple default. 1) The icon should show the actual date that we are on as does the Apple default calendar (ADC). This would make things so much easier to just know what date it is. and 2) There needs to be an option to view the month as a whole like the ADC. That function is really the main reason I haven't made the complete switch over to google's calendar. It is extremely useful and worth at least liking into the option of being able to view each month in its entirety, and then choose dates from those months to add reminders and events much like the ADC. I know it may seem to be copying them, but this Google app has so many other features, functional and aesthetically based, which means a whole lot. I mean to even to the point that I, as of now, currently use both Google's calendar and the ADC, merely because of the fact that the ACD allows me to view each month, all 12, especially useful is being able to go to the month after and the month ahead, just to check long term future scheduled events and also what date land on what day of the week. I know it's possible in Google's app but it is much more difficult and less user friendly. Otherwise, if those features could be fixed or added on, the ADC would be no more and just filed away in my folder of random apps I can't delete but will never use. I hope I don't have my foot in my mouth and there is a way to view full months in the way the ADC allows, in which case please help me figure out how because seriously, if these two points could be addressed and added to the features of Google's calendar, it really would be the perfect tool/app as a calendar for checking the date, scheduling events and just sharing organized overall and in general. I hope this isn't just a useless message and someone of some type of importance for Google reads this and decides that my ideas are valid and worth looking into. Regardless, great app and if these problems or rooms for improvement are addressed and taken care of, it will certainly be the last calendar app I ever use, especially since I am slresdy using literally almost all of google's other apps that are offered.

Out team is noble and spread across the US, the finally found the glitch and solved the problem by deleting the calendar and then reinstalling it but in the meantime, we lost out on a $75,000 client fee because non of us had the calendar invite that the company sent. title: It is decent
body:
My friend highly recommended this app and I can see why. The interface on my phone is easy to use and it syncs fairly fast with my computer. Everything is color coded and fits into their own "calendars" which is neat because then you can toggle certain events off. It is really simple to add a date and it mostly syncs with the iPhone calendar (I use both to keep track of my life). 

Unfortunately, I noticed that I cannot adjust calendars colors or even make new calendars, which is a problem. If I press on an event, I have to completely exit the app (swipe the app away) because there is no back button. If i make an event, I can't assign it to a calendar. I also don't get the cool images from the computer. What I can do on my phone is limited.

Overall though, Google calendar is efficient and effective for someone needing to keep organized but I would much rather be using It on my computer because you can do so much more there. You can add tasks to do on a side bar, you can make new calendars (and then add events to those calendars with the right color), you can expand or compress the screen (which is more of a phone screen size problem but if the app could change from portrait to landscape, that would be helpful), you can adjust notifications settings, you can adjust events easily...basically the computer version is very easy and comprehensive and better than the app.

title: Great for shared family calendar, but needs some improvement
body: My husband and I decided to use google calendar so that we could have access to each other's schedules and schedule family appointments/activities more easily. I love the many, many colors that are available to differentiate types of appointments (I use pink, my husband is blue, our shared events are green), but I am so disappointed that there is no month view of all events! The only month view that is available shows the days of the month, but not the number or types of appointments/activities scheduled for each day (like apple's calendar shows). I also don't like the way that google calendar adds locations. If I start typing an event and enter a location, if the location comes up on google maps, it automatically removes it from my event title. I have no problem with google adding the locations for me, but stop removing the words from my event title please! Also, if you don't have your phone contacts uploaded to your google account, google calendar's attempts to guess who you are planning events with can be pretty annoying. If you have everything synced to google already, I'm sure that feature would be very useful. But as a new mom of an infant, I need a calendar that saves me time, not makes me spend more of it getting contacts synced and researching how to tweak the minor issues I've found. I'll keep using it because it's the only way to coordinate my family's schedules,  but it would be so much better if they just made those small changes.

title: Awesome way to keep your schedule on check!
body:
The icon is clear, flat, beautifully designed, and right to the point
 The description on the app store is nice and clear. It explains what yu can use the app for
 and the features that make it different from other calendars, and maybe even better
 The app is really user friendly. It is really easy to reach all buttons on the app, and it is really to learn how
 to use it, and how it works, how you add new events and edit them.
 The target audience isn't defined on the description, but it really is implied, that it is for any user, no matter the age
 of the user, to keep track of their schedules and birthdays
 An innovative characteristic of the app is the ability for the user to change the way that their schedule is displayed, either in Schedule view, which displays your events linearly, or weekly view, which shows you your schedule in full view for the whole week. Additionally, doesn't matter which display you chose, you can pull up a monthly view above in half the screen to choose the day you want to jump to quickly.
 The app is really easy to navigate. All buttons are within reach and theres no buttons that at first glance you won't know what they are, or what they do.
 The app is completely free, and it doesnt have any ads.
 The app is professionaly sound. It looks professional, and it looks like they don't mean any funny business. It goes straight to the point, both design-wise and usability-wise
 The main focus of the app is to manage your schedule effectively. Be able to know when and where an appointment is, and be able to do so with simplicity.
 The design of the app is what you'd expect from Google, really nice flat design with nice full colors, which ties nicely with Google's Material design guide.
 Overall a really awesome app and would definitely recommend!

The maximum view is a 7 day/8 hour block. It doesn't notify you if a scheduled event is hidden. Say you're viewing Tue-Thu, 1pm-8pm & have an event on Wed at 11am. Guess what? There's no notification unless you scroll up! There's nothing to say "Hey! You have more events above/below!"

And the best part? It looks like it was designed by that special kid who's in dire need of a helmet. Those terribly bright but off colors are an embarrassment. My only conclusion is google is failing on purpose.

Oh, and thanks for getting rid of text alerts. It's not like anyone used it. Seriously, there is now ZERO reasons to use this mess of an app.

Calendars 5 is far superior & the best calendar app in the App Store, hands down.

title: Cmon Google Cal
body:
As a virtual assistant, I'm constantly using this app--here are the issues I have with it:

1. STOP automatically switching on Google Hangout to every invite-it's annoying and confusing to clients when I forget to switch it back off (which I shouldn't even have to do...)

2. On the desktop version of Google Calendar, when I type in the first letter of a name of any invite recipient, a whole list of names show up based on my email responses--why is it not like this for the app?? The names show up when titling the event, but that's not where I need it--I need it when I'm actually inviting guest to events/meetings. Going back and forth to copy and past email addresses from messages to this app is annoying to say the very least.

3. Where is the integration with the default Mail app on iOS 8?? Must I download gMail in order to tap and hold on a date directly in my email for a Google calendar option to pop up???

4. A notification bar widget would be nice...

Google devs, please if you have any mercy for a virtual assistant with carpal tunnel who needs more simplified means to the Google calendar app, please take these things into consideration and update accordingly.

title: Beta-stage buggy. Even after June 2015 update, no substantive noticeable improvements.
body:
1. With Google Calendar, if an event's All-day setting is Off, you switch that event's All-day setting to On, change the month of that event, then toggle the All-day setting back to Off, Google Calendar will revert the date back to what it was before you started the process.

2. Apple Calendar's icon shows day of the month and day of the week. Google just shows "31" no matter what the day of the week and date are.

3. Apple Calendar doesn't hide all-day events when you jump to the current date. Google won't display an entire day when you jump to current date. Instead, Google Calendar will scroll past all-day events depending on the time of day that you tap to display those all-day events, requiring you to scroll back up to see some all-day events - running the risk of missing some all-day events because the calendar didn't display them.

4. In Apple Calendar, Search is accessible with one tap. With Google Calendar, you have to hit menu, then Search.
Apple Calendar shows search results as you type. Google makes you type out the search then press Search.

5. Apple lets you copy a phone # by long pressing it. Google won't let you copy a phone #. If you long press a phone # in Google Calendar, it just dials the # without giving you an opportunity to copy it.

===

Things Google Calendar's better at:

1. Can automatically include links to all of a contact's phone #s and offer the option to dial each phone #.

2. Will open addresses in Google Maps. Apple Calendar opens addresses in Apple Maps.

title: Finally a REAL Google Calendar App For iOS
body:
If you’re a Google Calendar user who has been looking for a real, functional and FREE way to get full use of it on your iPhone, then look no further.

I started using my Google Calendar long before I ever got an iPhone. So when I got my iPhone, I was so steeped in Google Calendar that I had no desire to switch to iCal or put my calendar in the cloud, as much as I love Apple. I’ve tried Sunrise, CalenMob, CalenGoo, and my iPhone’s own calendar app, but none of these apps could get it quite right. Why? Because none of them were made by Google.

The app is beautiful, functional and VERY easy to use; even if you share your calendar or view shared calendars. It gives you access to advanced features like invitation management, calendar privacy and event colors. It even employs Google’s ever-impressive predictive technology to make entering events quick and easy.

Now, in the interest of full disclosure, I still run my iPhone calendar (with my Google account plugged into it) along side the Google Calendar app. I’ve been doing this for two reasons. First, to act as a backup in case the Google Calendar app crashes or fails (which it hasn’t). Second, because I want to be able to use Siri with the calendar and information in the Google Calendar app is not accessible by Siri and somehow I don’t see that happening. But the good news is, I don’t have to enter events twice. The iPhone Calendar app catches all the entries I make into the Google Calendar app.

In my humble opinion, this app does a fantastic job of bringing full, rich Google Calendar functionality to iOS.

title: Promising, but third-party calendars badly crippled
body:
It seems like a nice app, but it's significantly and seemingly arbitrarily crippled unless you're using a Google calendar. For instance, intelligent parsing of your event name to set time, contacts, location, etc, inexplicably only works with Google calendars. If you use any other calendar, you have to configure these fields manually. This seems like entirely client-side functionality that should in no way depend on the backend calendar provider. Other calendar apps (Fantastical, Tempo, to name just a couple) manage to provide these same features in a calendar-agnostic fashion. Things get even weirder. If you enter a location using a Google calendar, it displays a nice map and lets you tap the location for directions. Do the same for any other calendar, and not only do you not get the map, but the location field can't be tapped or even copied, making it pretty useless. Why on earth is the ability to tap a location to send it to maps calendar-specific?

The thing is, even if you use Google for your main calendar, lots of people have other calendars. I have an Exchange calendar for work, and a bunch of caldav subscriptions (Kayak trips, Zipcar reservations, holidays, various others). I couldn't convert these all to Google calendars if I wanted to, and the inability to use them properly in this app means I end up not being able to use it for my Google calendars. If Google wants to implement Google-specific features that require backend functionality not available in other calendars, that's fine, but seemingly intentionally degrading entirely client-side functionality for anything but its own calendars is extremely annoying.

author: DublinRanch

title: No shared rooms, no availability checking, no landscape
body:
Google, if you took this long to build an app, I had hoped it would have something of real value.  You have added Google Now-ish bells and whistles but your app fails in the most basic of capabilities.

I want to schedule a meeting and check a co-workers availability. Can’t do it with your app.

I want to see what conference rooms are available to book for my meeting. Can’t to it with your app

I want to turn my phone sideways and see a landscape view. Can’t do it with your app.

I want to be able to see my whole week and not just 3 days. Can’t do it with your app.

Your blog post says “It’s about time.” Actually, it is “Too little, too late."

title: Very nice calendar app
body:
It's beautifully designed and making a new event is super easy. I love that there's a search function and it works with most calendars like Apples and Microsofts, rather than limiting it to Google. 
A small issue is the 3 day view. Event titles don't fit in the column, which leaves half the event title unreadable. This forces you to switch to another view or click on the event. I also don't see a way to change the default calendar where the event is places. I think I'll stay using Sunrise calendar app and check this app out at a future time.
